design.text: Phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, multicenter, 52-week trial; subjects randomized 2:1 to seladelpar 10 mg or placebo, stratified by baseline ALP and presence of pruritus.

citations.quote: Trial CB8025-32048 is a phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial evaluating seladelpar 10 mg daily versus placebo in adult subjects with PBC and an inadequate response to or an intolerance to UDCA.
Eligible subjects were randomized in a 2:1 ratio to receive seladelpar 10 mg or matching placebo orally QD for the duration of the trial.
Trial 32048 was a double-blind, placebo-controlled, 52-week trial which randomized 193 subjects in a 2:1 ratio to receive seladelpar 10mg or placebo.

Subjects were randomized to receive seladelpar 10 mg (n=128) or placebo (n=65) in a 2:1 ratio, stratified by baseline ALP (<350 U/L versus \ge350 U/L) and presence of pruritus (baseline average pruritus NRS score <4 versus \ge4).

population.text: Adults with PBC with an inadequate response to or intolerance of UDCA; enrolled subjects had ALP ≥ 1.67 × ULN and TB ≤ 2 × ULN, excluding other chronic liver diseases or history of hepatic decompensation.

citations.quote: Enrolled subjects with PBC had an ALP \ge 1.67 \times ULN and TB \le 2 \times ULN. Subjects were excluded from the trial if they had other chronic liver diseases or a history of hepatic decompensation events.

endpoint.text: Primary endpoint: proportion achieving biochemical response at Month 12, defined as ALP < 1.67 × ULN, an ALP decrease of at least 15% from baseline, and TB ≤ ULN.

citations.quote: Efficacy determination was based on the proportion of subjects who achieved a biochemical response at month 12, defined as ALP < 1.67 \times ULN, an ALP decrease of at least 15% from baseline, and TB \le ULN.

n.text: 193 subjects randomized 2:1 to seladelpar 10 mg (n=128) or placebo (n=65).

result.text: At Month 12, 62% of seladelpar subjects vs 20% of placebo achieved a biochemical response (treatment difference 42%; 95% CI 28%, 53%). ALP normalization occurred in 25% of seladelpar subjects vs none on placebo (difference 25%; CI 18%, 33%).

citations.quote: At Month 12, 62% of subjects who received seladelpar compared with 20% of subjects who received placebo achieved a biochemical response, for a treatment difference of 42% (95% CI:28%, 53%).
In addition, 25% of subjects who received seladelpar compared with none who received placebo achieved ALP normalization, for a treatment difference of 25% (CI: 18%, 33%).

indication.text: Treatment of primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) in combination with UDCA in adults who have an inadequate response to UDCA, or as monotherapy in patients unable to tolerate UDCA. Approved under accelerated approval based on reduction of ALP.

citations.quote: LIVDELZI is a peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR)-delta agonist indicated for the treatment of primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) in combination with ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) in adults who have an inadequate response to UDCA, or as monotherapy in patients unable to tolerate UDCA.
This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on a reduction of alkaline phosphatase (ALP).

target_moa.text: Seladelpar is a selective peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR)-delta agonist; its exact mechanism in PBC is unknown, but inhibition of bile acid synthesis through activation of PPAR-delta may be relevant to its therapeutic effect.

citations.quote: Seladelpar is a selective PPAR delta (PPAR\delta) agonist.

Mechanism of action	Seladelpar's exact mechanism of action is unknown. Inhibition of bile acid synthesis through activation of PPARδ may be potentially relevant to therapeutic effects of seladelpar in the treatment of PBC.

modality.text: Small molecule (first-in-class new molecular entity, PPAR-delta agonist).

citations.quote: Seladelpar, a first-in-class new molecular entity, is a PPAR-delta agonist.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥5% and higher than placebo) were headache (8% vs 3%), abdominal pain (7% vs 2%), nausea (6% vs 5%), abdominal distension (6% vs 3%), and dizziness (5% vs 2%). Fractures occurred in 4% (n=5) of LIVDELZI-treated patients vs none on placebo.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Biochemical surrogate endpoint of reduction of ALP (ALP ≤ 1.67 × ULN with ≥15% reduction) and normalization of total bilirubin (TB < ULN), accepted as reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

citations.quote: This application is approved under accelerated approval based on a biochemical response of reduction of ALP and normalization of TB.

DHN has accepted ALP \le 1.67 \times ULN and TB < ULN as a reasonably likely surrogate endpoint to support accelerated approval. Because there can be spontaneous fluctuations in ALP, a threshold of at least 15% reduction in ALP was added to ensure that reduction was related to treatment effect and not due to variability in ALP.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Trial CB8025-41837, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial enrolling 192 subjects with PBC and compensated cirrhosis, followed up to 3 years for a composite clinical endpoint of liver decompensation, liver transplant, and all-cause mortality.

citations.quote: Trial CB8025-41837 is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial which will enroll a total of 192 subjects with PBC with compensated cirrhosis. Subjects will be followed for up to 3 years to assess a composite clinical endpoint of liver decompensation, liver transplant, and all-cause mortality.

summary.text: LIVDELZI (seladelpar) received Orphan Drug Designation (2016) and Breakthrough Therapy Designation (2019) for PBC, was reviewed as a Priority NDA, and was granted accelerated approval based on the biochemical surrogate endpoint of ALP reduction and TB normalization, with continued approval contingent on confirmatory Trial CB8025-41837.

citations.quote: On November 7, 2016, MBX-8025 was granted Orphan Drug Designation for treatment of PBC.

On December 20, 2018, the Sponsor submitted a BTDR. On February 14, 2019, seladelpar was granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation (BTD) for the treatment of early-stage primary PBC in combination with UDCA in adults with an inadequate response to UDCA, or as monotherapy in adults unable to tolerate UDCA.
This application is approved under accelerated approval based on a biochemical response of reduction of ALP and normalization of TB.

Continued approval for this indication will be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trials. Specifically, Trial CB8025-41837 is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial which will enroll a total of 192 subjects with PBC with compensated cirrhosis.

requirement.text: 4645-1 Complete Trial CB8025-41837, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to evaluate the effect of seladelpar on clinical outcomes in subjects with primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) and compensated cirrhosis. Efficacy must be demonstrated using a composite endpoint of mortality, liver transplant, MELD >= 15, ascites requiring treatment, and hospitalization for hepatic decompensation (e.g., variceal bleeding, hepatic encephalopathy, and spontaneous bacterial peritonitis).

citations.quote: 4645-1 Complete Trial CB8025-41837, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to evaluate the effect of seladelpar on clinical outcomes in subjects with primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) and compensated cirrhosis. requirement.text: 4645-2 Conduct a ten-year worldwide descriptive study that collects prospective and retrospective data from women exposed to seladelpar during pregnancy and/or lactation to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications, adverse effects on the developing fetus and neonate, and adverse effects on the infant. Infant outcomes will be assessed through at least the first year of life. The minimum number of patients should be specified in the protocol.

requirement.text: 4645-3 Perform a lactation study, milk only, in lactating women who have received seladelpar to measure concentrations of seladelpar in breast milk using a validated assay and to assess the effects on the breastfed infant.
